Usage: ni convert <sources...> -o <output> [options]

Convert capture files between formats (frame-level, no protocol parsing).

Arguments:
  <sources...>          One or more source files or specs

Options:
  -o, --output          Output file path (required)
  --output-format, -f   Output format spec (see below; overrides extension)
  --overwrite           Replace an existing output (otherwise an existing output is an error)
  -n, --max-frames      Maximum number of frames to convert
  --split-size <MB>     Split when exporter EstimatedOutputBytes reaches this size (MiB; live, no FS probe)
  --split-count <N>     Split output every N frames
  --filter <expr>       Only keep packets matching this filter expression
                        (frames are parsed only when a filter is set)
  --profile <name>      Settings profile (must exist; 'default' is created on first use)
  --settings-path <dir> Base directory for settings storage
  --set <key>=<value>   Override one setting for this run only, e.g. --set settings.maxFileSize=1GiB (repeatable;
                        a limit takes a number with a unit, or off; see ni settings describe --limits)
  --blf-cache-size <MB> Container cache budget for BLF sources (MiB)
  --progress <N>        Report progress every N frames
  --tolerant            Skip malformed frames instead of aborting
  --verbose             Print the parse work chosen for the run (parse: none | fields only, no tree (…) | field tree (…))
  -h, --help            Show this help message

Output format is auto-detected from the output extension (plugins add more; see 'ni plugins list'):
  .pcapng / other       PCAPNG (default)
  .blf                  BLF with default compression
  .asc                  CANalyzer ASCII log (CAN, CAN FD, CAN XL, LIN, FlexRay, Ethernet)
                        AFDX data frames are read. AFDX status, AFDX bus statistics, ETH STAT, and ETH RxEr are not read.

Output format specifications (--output-format):
  pcapng                PCAPNG format
  blf                   BLF, defaul

Usage: ni settings <command> [options]

Read and change the application settings and the settings of a profile (plugin settings included).

Commands:
  list  [--scope application|profile|all] [--group <group>] [--json]
  get   <name> [--scope application|profile] [--group <group>]
  set   <name> <value> [--scope application|profile] [--group <group>]
  reset <name> [--scope application|profile]    Remove the stored value; the default applies
  describe <name> [--format text|json]          What a setting is; for a limit what it bounds and why
  describe --limits [--format text|json|markdown]   Every limit with value, default, unit, and range

Options:
  --profile <name>      Settings profile (must exist; 'default' is created on first use)
  --settings-path <dir> Base directory for settings storage
  --set <key>=<value>   Override one setting for this run only, e.g. --set settings.maxFileSize=1GiB (repeatable;
                        not allowed with set and reset; a limit takes a number with a unit, or off)
  -h, --help            Show this help message

Values: true/false, numbers, hex bytes (0A1B), enumeration names, text, and arrays as JSON ([1,2]) or comma lists.
Relative paths in plugins.paths are stored as full paths. A stored value of a plugin that is not loaded is JSON.

  -h, --help                    Show this help message

Names: 1 to 256 letters, digits, spaces, dots, dashes, and underscores; not application, logs, plugins,
